readiness.mainReason: No blocking rule fired: the deck names the decision, answers it, sources its core claims and marks its load-bearing assumption as the thing to test, so the core is sound and only refinements remain.
readiness.highestRiskIssue: Slide 8 projects about 5,000 pounds in year one but never sizes that against grants being 80% of income on slide 3, so the deck does not show how much of the gap membership actually closes.
readiness.whatCouldChangeIt: Actual conversion rates for the three comparable groups, or a pounds figure for the grant shortfall, would sharpen the case, but neither changes the deliberately small-start recommendation.

dimensions.name: Client decision usefulness
dimensions.note: The decision, the answer and the first action are stated plainly and early.

dimensions.name: Problem framing
dimensions.note: The problem is specific and held consistently, but success for the diversification goal is defined only at the pilot level, not against the income gap.

dimensions.name: Storyline and pyramid logic
dimensions.note: The governing insight is on slide 1 and every section feeds it, problem to evidence to recommendation to first steps.

dimensions.name: Evidence quality
dimensions.note: Core claims trace to named sources and the one projection is labelled an assumption to test.

dimensions.name: Analysis and insight
dimensions.note: Findings feed the recommendation, but the projected income is not compared to the size of the grant shortfall it is meant to address.

dimensions.name: Recommendation specificity
dimensions.note: The action, the owner, the timing and the success trigger are all named on slide 10.

dimensions.name: Feasibility and implementation
dimensions.note: The plan fits existing capacity, sequences the steps and starts with a soft launch to 200 contacts.

dimensions.name: Risks, assumptions and uncertainty
dimensions.note: The load-bearing conversion assumption and the main risk are named and the soft launch tests them.

dimensions.name: Slide-level communication
dimensions.note: Each slide carries one message that its content supports, but several titles such as The numbers and First steps are topic labels not assertions.

dimensions.name: Professionalism, tone and confidentiality
dimensions.note: Professional throughout, the coordinator is named by role not judged, and certainty is calibrated.

strengths.point: The deck answers the client question first, in the title, so a busy reader knows the recommendation before slide 2.
strengths.quote: Client E should launch a paid membership scheme, starting with a single tier in the autumn.

strengths.point: The key projection is handled honestly, flagged as an assumption and named as the thing to test rather than presented as fact.
strengths.quote: The 8% assumption is conservative against the 32% attendance rate and is the main thing to test.

strengths.point: The first steps are specific with an owner, a sequence and a measurable go or no-go trigger.
strengths.quote: Month three: full launch if the soft launch clears 5%.

strengths.point: The core claims driving the case are sourced to named internal records.
strengths.quote: Project grants are 80% of Client E's income (2024 accounts) and each is single-year.

findings.title: The projected membership income is never compared to the size of the grant shortfall it is meant to close.
findings.principle: Analysis and insight: connect the result to the size of the problem it solves.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 3 sets the problem as grants being 80% of income with two of five not expected to renew. Slide 8 projects about 5,000 pounds in year one. The deck never states what fraction of the lost grant income that recovers, so the reader cannot see whether membership is a meaningful hedge or a first small experiment.

evidence.quote: If 8% of the mailing list joins at 45 pounds, that is about 5,000 pounds in year one.
Project grants are 80% of Client E's income (2024 accounts) and each is single-year.

findings.why: The client asked how to diversify income. Without sizing the gap the deck cannot say whether membership alone is enough or whether other streams are needed alongside it.
findings.reflect: In pounds, how large is the shortfall from the two grants that may not renew, and what share of it does 5,000 pounds cover.
findings.fix: Add the shortfall in pounds and state what share year-one membership recovers, then frame membership as the first of possibly several streams if the share is small. This strengthens an already-sound small-start recommendation, it does not change it.

findings.title: The 8% conversion assumption is checked against attendance but not against what comparable groups actually convert.
findings.principle: Evidence quality: benchmark a load-bearing assumption against the closest available comparator.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 5 cites the comparable groups only for pricing. Slide 8 justifies the 8% conversion against Client E's own 32% attendance rate. The nearest external anchor, what those comparable groups convert from their own audiences, is not used, so the assumption rests on a single internal proxy.

evidence.quote: The 8% assumption is conservative against the 32% attendance rate and is the main thing to test.
Three comparable local arts non-profits run membership at 40 to 60 pounds a year (their public websites, 2025).

findings.why: A conversion figure grounded in one internal proxy is easier for a funder to question than one triangulated against real peers, and the soft launch is cheaper to plan if the target is anchored.
findings.reflect: What conversion rate do the three comparable groups achieve, and does that raise or lower confidence in 8%.
findings.fix: Where the comparators publish membership numbers, add their approximate conversion as a second anchor for the 8% target. Keep the soft launch as the real test either way.

findings.title: Several slide titles are topic labels rather than the assertion the slide makes.
findings.principle: Minto action titles: the title carries the message so the titles alone tell the story.
findings.diagnosis: The opening and closing titles assert (slide 1, slide 6), but middle titles such as The numbers and First steps name a topic rather than the point the slide proves. A reader skimming only the titles gets the recommendation but not the supporting logic.
findings.why: A partner or board member who reads only the titles should be able to reconstruct the argument. Topic labels force them back into the body to find the point.
findings.reflect: If a reader saw only your titles, could they state the point of slide 8 and slide 10.
findings.fix: Rewrite the topic-label titles as complete-sentence assertions that state the takeaway, for example what the numbers show and what the first step commits to. This is polish on a deck whose argument already holds.

comments.problem: The member benefits are asserted to use existing capacity but two members-only events a year are not sized against staff time.
comments.why: Slide 9 names staff strain as an assumption, so the benefit slide and the risk slide should agree on the load.
comments.fix: Note the rough staff hours the two events need so the no-strain assumption is visible where the benefits are promised.

questionsForLead: Do we know the actual conversion rate of the three comparable groups, or only their pricing.
How large is the grant shortfall in pounds, and does about 5,000 pounds in year one meaningfully diversify against it.
Was any income stream beyond membership considered, or was membership the only option in scope for this project.

learningNote.lesson: A recommendation should size its result against the problem it is solving. A clean projection means little until the reader knows what share of the gap it closes.
learningNote.weakHabit: Presenting a well-built number in isolation without tying it back to the magnitude of the original problem.
learningNote.exercise: For the headline result, write one sentence: this recovers X of the Y we are trying to replace. If you cannot fill in Y, that is the next number to find.

notAssessed: Whether the 8% conversion assumption is realistic. No comparable conversion data was provided, only pricing.
The size of the grant shortfall in pounds. The deck gives a percentage of income, not an amount.
Visual design, layout and charts. Only slide text was provided.
Whether the coordinator has capacity to own the launch alongside current duties. The deck does not say.

callouts.label: Income not sized to the grant gap
